reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: I read the output contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, RiskAssessment resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and the supplied behavior reports. I also checked the local R4/R6 StructureDefinition evidence behind the main element changes and searched the behavior reports for RiskAssessment-specific findings. The deterministic aggregate was treated as prior context only and compared after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 RiskAssessment was trial-use/FMM 1, so the base specification carried weak stability pressure compared with mature or normative resources. That softens the standards burden for adopting CodeableReference and additive model improvements, but it does not make clinical explanation, probability interpretation, status lifecycle, or audit attribution irrelevant for implementations that used the resource.

overall.oneLineConclusion: RiskAssessment keeps its resource identity and is mostly stable; affected instances need a targeted reason-field transform, so additional avoidable breaks should still be judged per change.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual migration shape is not a resource replacement or broad remodel. R6 keeps `StructureDefinition/RiskAssessment` with the same canonical URL, kind, type, and DomainResource base. The one direct R4-to-R6 instance break is local: R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` were replaced by R6 `reason` using `CodeableReference`. The other reviewed structural changes widen the model for R6 content: additional Observation status codes, Patient/RelatedPerson performers, and `probabilityQuantity`.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: A RiskAssessment-specific migration program is not already unavoidable at the resource level. Existing R4 instances without `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` remain structurally close to R6. Instances using those fields need a predictable transform to `reason.concept` or `reason.reference`, and R6-to-R4 downgrade needs policy for a `CodeableReference` containing both children. The status, performer, and probability changes are mostly reverse-version or generated-code chores for new R6 content, not old-valid/new-invalid breaks.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because there is no removed resource, no required new element, no local cardinality narrowing, and no direct RiskAssessment behavior/API finding, compatibility preservation remains high-leverage on a per-change basis. The existing reason break does not make further breaks free: each new rename, removal, or narrowing would still add avoidable migration work. At the same time, the R4 FMM 1 baseline and the duplicate-representation cost of keeping old reason fields mean the current local hard break is better handled as a targeted transform plus guidance rather than as proof of a broad resource redesign failure.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The main less-breaking base alternative would have been to retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding preferred `reason`. That would preserve old wire instances, but it would create two representations for the same reason, conflict and precedence rules, search/codegen duplication, and unclear pairing behavior. For `status`, `performer`, and `probability[x]`, R6 mostly widens the base model while preserving R4-valid content; avoiding those additions would protect R4-only consumers of new R6 data but would also block legitimate R6 expressivity. No local finding presents a clearly low-cost base-compatible alternative that should dominate the resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The supplied behavior reports contain no direct findings whose affected resources include `RiskAssessment`. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings, including Resource-level operations and shared search metadata, may affect generic R6 migration tooling, but RiskAssessment is not itself `Resource` or `DomainResource`, so they are context only and do not drive this resource-level judgment.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate headline: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No`, `resourceMigrationShape = mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and `compatibilityLeverage = preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The nuance is that the reason merge is a real targeted local remodel, not just a trivial countable break; however, it is isolated, optional, semantically mappable in the forward direction, and on an FMM 1 resource, so it still does not make a resource-wide migration program unavoidable.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural facts because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were available locally and the behavior reports had no RiskAssessment-specific matches. Remaining uncertainty is about official rationale, final R6 ballot evolution, exact terminology downgrade policy for new Observation status codes, and real-world prevalence of `reasonCode`, `reasonReference`, or probability values in production RiskAssessment exchange.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 reasonCode and reasonReference were replaced by R6 reason
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only direct old-valid/new-invalid instance break and therefore the main reason the resource is not `low-material-change`. It still looks like a targeted local migration rather than a resource-wide redesign: the old code and reference content maps naturally to `CodeableReference.concept` or `.reference`, the reference target set is preserved, and the resource identity remains stable. It matters for clinical explanation and audit, especially for reverse conversion where paired concept/reference content can lose association.

findingConsiderations.title: RiskAssessment.status required binding uses expanded R6 Observation Status codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Status is mandatory and lifecycle-significant, so R6-to-R4 downgrade and enum/parser compatibility need explicit handling for new codes such as `appended` or `cannot-be-obtained`. It does not drive a major migration conclusion because the R6 binding appears to retain the R4 codes, so old RiskAssessment instances are not invalidated on this path.

findingConsiderations.title: prediction.probability[x] adds Quantity and a percent Quantity invariant
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Probability is central when present, and `probabilityQuantity` can be lossy when downgraded to R4 decimal, especially for comparators or extensions. But R6 keeps the R4 decimal and Range choices and constrains only the new Quantity branch, so this is a reverse-version/codegen migration chore rather than an old-valid/new-invalid resource break.

findingConsiderations.title: RiskAssessment.performer can now reference Patient or RelatedPerson
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a target-list widening. It can matter for attribution and R6-to-R4 downgrade policy, but it preserves all R4 performer targets and is optional. It therefore has little weight in deciding whether a RiskAssessment migration program is already unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search metadata change can affect generated clients and conformance tooling across many resource types, including clients that also search for RiskAssessment resources. It is not a RiskAssessment-specific search finding in the supplied reports and was not scored as a resource-level driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared Resource operation removals are important for generic server/client migration, but they apply through the base Resource surface rather than through RiskAssessment's local content model. They do not change the conclusion that RiskAssessment itself is mostly stable with one local hard break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or verify a simple RiskAssessment R4-to-R6 mapping for `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` to `reason.concept` and `reason.reference`, including explicit reverse-conversion policy when one R6 `CodeableReference` contains both concept and reference.
Define downgrade and test policy for R6-only content: new Observation status codes, `probabilityQuantity` with percent/comparator/extension cases, and Patient or RelatedPerson performers.

Keep future RiskAssessment compatibility review per-change. A new local rename, removal, required element, narrowing, or direct behavior break should not be discounted merely because the existing reason transform already exists.
Handle shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search metadata changes in the cross-resource migration plan rather than duplicating them as RiskAssessment-specific findings.

caveats: No official RiskAssessment R4-to-R6 diff, ballot rationale, or work-group migration note was present in the local inputs.
No official terminology expansion or ConceptMap was available for ObservationStatus or for RiskAssessment-specific downgrade policy.
The R6 source is 6.0.0-ballot4, so final R6 content may change.
The behavior reports had no direct RiskAssessment-specific findings; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was considered only as context.
